It can go first, with a comma, or after, as a final reservation: “Me encanta correr, aunque me cuesta madrugar”. It also works in the past: “Aunque llovía, salimos a correr”.

yd5sap: In a real or possible condition, “si” is always followed by the present indicative. What changes is the result, depending on your intention: a general truth or a habit (present), a prediction or a promise (future or “ir a”), an instruction (imperative), a permission or an obligation (“poder”, “tener que”).
gze2u6: Never use the future or the present subjunctive after this “si”. Also distinguish “si” from “cuando”: “si llueve” leaves the possibility open; “cuando llueva” takes for granted that it will rain (and takes the subjunctive, as you saw in week 6). When “si” means “whether” (“no sé si…”), it does allow the future: “No sé si llegaré a la meta”.

1e99cck: The conditional: an easy form and twelve irregulars

ufh1ml: All the forms have an accent on the “í”. Careful: the imperfect of -er and -ir verbs has the same endings, but without the “r” of the infinitive: “corría” (imperfect) versus “correría” (conditional).

142beic: “Correría” or “corría”: the “r” that separates the conditional from the imperfect
16oj52r: In -er and -ir verbs, the conditional and the imperfect are very similar: “corría / correría”, “salía / saldría”, “tenía / tendría”. 1igyvj6: In both forms the “í” is stressed and forms a hiatus with the “a”: co-rre-RÍ-a, co-RRÍ-a. Don’t turn it into a diphthong (“correrya”); pronounce two clear syllables at the end. In “-ríamos” the stress stays on the “í”: co-rre-RÍ-a-mos.
1az0ncy: All conditional forms have an accent on the “í” because it breaks the diphthong: entrenaría, tendríamos, saldrían.

1yngn13: The Corredores de la Malagueta club hands out this guide to people who are going to run their first half marathon.
k8nkey: Running 21 kilometres seems crazy when you start. However, every year hundreds of beginners cross the finish line on the Paseo del Parque, and most of them are not athletes. Although you don’t have to suffer to improve, you do need consistency: if you go running four times a week for three months, your body will adapt.
1apmsud: The most frequent doubts have simple answers. If something hurts for more than two days, stop running and see a physiotherapist. If it’s very hot, train early or at sunset. If one day you feel you have no energy, you can walk for a while: walking is not failing. And if you get bored of always running alone, join our Wednesday evening runs, which start by the lighthouse.
jx769s: And our advice for the big day? If we were you, we would have a light dinner the night before and arrive at the start forty minutes early. We wouldn’t change anything either: not breakfast, not clothes, not trainers. Many runners tell us afterwards that, in a second race, they would go more slowly at the beginning.
13ud5va: Finally, a request: could you let us know if you drop out of the plan? Although we completely understand, we would like to know so we can give your place to someone else.
